sentences.text:
For Respondent(s) : Mr. Urja Ram Kalbi, P. P.
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SANJEET PUROHIT Order 02/04/2026 1.

This application for bail has been filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 in connection with FIR No.13/2023, registered at Cyber Police Station Rajsamand for the offences under Sections 419, 420, 406 & 120B of IPC and Sections 66, 66D of Information and Technology Act.
2. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the accused- applicant has been falsely implicated in this case.
He, however, invited Court's attention towards the fact that contents of FIR show that applicant's name was not mentioned in it and thus, it shows no direct involvement of the applicant.
3. Learned counsel also submits that after conclusion of the investigation, the police has submitted challan in the matter.
He further submits that the accused-applicant is in custody since 25.01.2026 and he is no more required for any kind of interrogation and recovery.
(Uploaded on 02/04/2026 at 08:46:03 PM)
Learned counsel for the applicant states that the applicant is behind the bars for an offence which is triable by the Magistrate.

He further submits that no case of like nature is pending against the applicant and the trial will take its own time, therefore the accused-applicant may be released on bail Banti Babal vs State Of Rajasthan (2026:Rj-Jd:15152) on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152506432/

sentences.text: 1 5. Learned Public Prosecutor vehemently opposed the bail application.
The accused-applicant is involved in Cyber fraud cases by which more than Rs.1,50,000/- has been credited in his account.

He further submits that the present case is of Cyber fraud, which is treated as a serious criminal offence and, therefore, the applicant should not be enlarged on bail.
6.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.

7. Having regard to the totality of facts and circumstances of the case, considering the fact that offences alleged are triable by Magistrate, challan has already been filed; and that name of the applicant was not mentioned in the FIR; so also conclusion of the trial is going to take a considerable time, coupled with the fact that accused-applicant is in custody since 25.01.2026 and no useful purpose would be served by his continued incarceration, without expressing any opinion on the merits/demerits of the case, I deem it just and proper to grant bail to the accused- applicant.
8. Consequently, the bail application filed under Section 483 BNSS, 2023 is allowed.

The accused-applicant Banti Babal S/o Omaram Bishnoi arrested in connection with FIR No.13/2023,
Police Station Rajsamand shall be released on bail on his

(Uploaded on 02/04/2026 at 08:46:03 PM) [2026:RJ-JD:15152] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-1872/2026] furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the trial Court.
Applicant shall be required to appear before that Court on all dates of hearing and as and when called upon to do so.
9. The accused-applicant is also directed to mark his presence on 25th of every month till conclusion of trial before the concerned Police Station.
SHO of the concerned Police Station shall send the presence report of the accused-applicant to learned trial Court every month.
In case of any breach to the above condition, learned counsel for the State shall be free to move the application against the accused-applicant for cancellation of bail before concerned Magistrate.
10. Copy of this order also be sent to concerned SHO for compliance.
11. Needless to mention that the above observations made by this Court are on the basis of material so far produced before the Court.

These are only prima-facie observations and the same shall however, not come in the way of the trial Court to take independent view of the matter, based on ocular and oral evidence, while finally deciding the case.

(SANJEET PUROHIT),J 38-A.Arora/-
